content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes.
- Overestimates in the middle-to-late period following a spike, suggesting delayed correction or failure to capture mean reversion.
- Tends to overreact to recent high prices, leading to overshoots in forecasted values.
- Underestimates low-price periods, particularly when prices are falling sharply.
- Shows persistent lag in adjusting to true price movements, especially in the first 5–10 days of the forecast window.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — forecasts often remain too far from historical mean for extended periods.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the early days, then become more aggressive as the horizon progresses, creating a “sawtooth” pattern.
- High volatility in the forecast is not matched by true volatility — model underestimates volatility spikes and overestimates calm periods.
